$comment: ★★★ A FOREIGN ARCHIVE MEMBER READS THE PROGRAM'S DATA THROUGH THE GOT (P68 round 11: D-LK-ELF-READER-REFUSES-GOTPCREL-BLOCKS-REAL-GLIBC-MEMBERS — the x86_64 GOTPCREL / GOTPCRELX / REX_GOTPCRELX half, and D-LK-ELF-AARCH64-EXEC-REFUSES-GOT-RELOCATIONS — the aarch64 ADR_GOT_PAGE + LD64_GOT_LO12_NC half). The prebuilt archives hold three gcc 13.3 -O2 members each (the sources and flags are quoted in main.c): between them the x86_64 archive carries every GOT-slot-relative type gcc writes, and the aarch64 one the GOT pair for a datum, an element address, a function address and a call. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24 on main's build before this change: the x86_64 archive was refused at READ ('relocation type 42 ... is not declared') and the aarch64 one at the link's kind unifier ('relocation kind 7 ... is not declared by object format elf64-aarch64-linux-exec'); gcc -no-pie and -pie, clang 18 and aarch64 gcc under qemu link each archive with this main.c to 42. The link now lowers each GOT reference to a direct reference to a slot it mints, filled like any pointer-holding datum; no instruction is relaxed. What each value proves by the exit code: 1-3 — the default member's datum, element address, function address; 4 — the -fno-plt member's call through the GOT; 5-7 — the plain-GOTPCREL member's three; 42 = 17 + 25 + 0 only if every reference reached its definition. The `release` arm links the same archive under the shipped release pipeline.

The witness is a definition's own name.

aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -c`, `-O2 -fPIC -fno-plt -c` and `-O2 -fPIC -c` of the same three files + aarch64-linux-gnu-ar `rcs`: eight R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE + R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC pairs. The witness is a definition's own name.
